Analytical stance under test: kv-cache-dtype-and-quantization-interaction-first - the KV cache is a separate precision axis that must be held fixed.

Falsifiable hypothesis H198a: the KV cache dtype and any KV quantization setting are byte-for-byte identical across arms, verified by dumping the engine's effective KV dtype, per-block byte size and any KV quantization scale configuration from each live serving process. If they differ, the comparison confounds weight precision with KV precision and neither the memory ledger nor the quality delta can be attributed to weight-only quantization.

Weight-only quantization is defined by leaving activations and the KV cache alone, yet many quantization toolchains and serving presets change the KV dtype at the same time, either because a preset bundles them or because a lower KV precision is enabled to exploit the freed memory. That single coupling invalidates the entire study, because KV precision moves both the memory ledger and the quality result through a completely different mechanism than weight precision. Separate the axes explicitly. Dump from each live process the effective KV dtype, the per-block KV byte size, whether KV quantization is enabled and with which scale granularity, and assert equality across arms; then, if KV quantization is genuinely of interest, run it as a third arm rather than folding it into the quantized arm. The mechanisms differ in ways that matter operationally. Weight error is fixed at build time and identical for every request, so its damage is stationary and can be certified once per artefact. KV error accumulates along the sequence and interacts with attention softmax sharpness, so its damage grows with context length and is largest exactly in the long-context regime that memory savings are usually sought to serve. A study that conflates them will observe a quality delta that looks context-dependent and will misattribute it to weights. Boundary condition: where the deployment serves short contexts almost exclusively, KV precision contributes little to either memory or quality and the confound is small, but that must be shown from the served context-length distribution rather than assumed. ESTIMATE: KV pool bytes scale as two times layer count times KV head count times head dimension times total cached tokens times bytes per element, so halving KV element bytes changes the memory ledger by roughly the same order as the weight saving at long context; derivation is byte counting over the KV layout, and it is an ESTIMATE, not MEASURED. Rollback gate: if the runtime dumps disagree on any KV precision property, the run is void and must be re-executed with the axes separated.



--- Shared substrate (identical across this study, stated once so the stance above is the only variable) ---

Mechanism. Weight-only quantization (WOQ) reduces the BYTES OF WEIGHTS READ PER FORWARD PASS. It therefore helps only where the kernel is memory-bandwidth bound, which in LLM serving means small-batch autoregressive decode. Prefill is compute bound; dequantization adds arithmetic there, so TTFT is flat or slightly worse. As batch size rises, decode GEMMs become compute bound too and the advantage decays monotonically toward 1.0x. Any claim of a uniform speedup across the concurrency range is mechanically wrong and should be treated as an instrumentation bug until explained.

Byte-count ceiling (ESTIMATE, derivation inline, not a throughput result). A 9B-parameter model in BF16 is 9e9 x 2 B = 18 GB of weights. INT4 with group-128 FP16 scale and zero point costs about 0.5 + ~0.06 B/param, i.e. ~5.0-5.3 GB. Ratio ~3.2-3.6x. This is pure byte counting with no kernel-efficiency model and no attention or KV traffic included; it is an upper bound on batch-1 decode speedup ONLY. Applying Amdahl with a decode-weight-read fraction f: f=0.4 bounds end-to-end gain near 1.33x, f=0.8 near 2.1x (ESTIMATE).

Mandatory two-arm-plus-one design. Run the quantized configuration TWICE: (a) with KV cache block count clamped to the BF16 baseline's block count, which isolates the kernel/bandwidth effect; (b) at native capacity, which shows the deployable benefit. Freed HBM becomes additional KV blocks and raises throughput by batching alone. If the clamped arm is flat, the honest conclusion is "we bought KV headroom", and tuning KV settings on the BF16 arm must be priced as the cheaper alternative before shipping a second numeric path.

Arm identity is frozen and hashed. Checkpoint hash, bit width, group size, symmetric/asymmetric, outlier or mixed-precision policy, calibration dataset hash, library and engine build, TP/PP layout, activation precision, KV precision, block size, max_num_seqs, max_model_len, chunked-prefill state, speculative-decoding state. The configuration symmetric difference between arms must be exactly the bit-width fields; anything else invalidates the comparison. Weight-only means weight-only: "INT4 plus FP8 KV" is two experiments, and the KV change usually explains most of the throughput delta while none of the quality delta gets attributed correctly.

Comparison point. Compare arms at the intersection of each arm's own latency-throughput frontier with the p95 SLO, never at a fixed batch size; the two arms have different optimal batch sizes, and fixed-batch comparison is the single most common way these studies mislead. Cost unit is GPU-seconds per 1,000 output tokens at that fixed p95 SLO, converted to currency last.

Measurement protocol. At least five concurrency points, at least three repeats per point, steady state with a fixed warmup-exclusion rule, greedy decoding and fixed seed for quality, bootstrap 95% CIs on ABSOLUTE quality deltas. Quality is sliced: long context, structured/JSON output, code, math, safety and refusal behaviour; aggregate scores can stay flat while repetition or truncation degrades, so sampled side-by-side output diffs are part of the evidence, not a nicety. A BF16-vs-BF16 A/A control across seeds and physical GPUs establishes the noise floor that any claimed delta must clear.

Confounders to control and report. Autotune cache warmth; clock and thermal drift over long runs; asymmetric telemetry overhead; prefill/decode mix drift between arms; silent kernel fallback to a dequantize-then-GEMM path (dump per-layer kernel names and timings and diff the arms - a null result with a fallback in the logs is a tooling defect, not a verdict on the method); calibration-set leakage into the eval set, disproved by hash comparison; library defaults silently changing group size across versions.

Evidence required before any decision. Per-request raw records (arrival, TTFT, per-token timestamps, output length, status); per-layer kernel name and achieved-bandwidth traces for both arms; the arm configuration manifest with hashes; per-slice quality scores with CIs plus raw generations; the HBM ledger with KV blocks as the residual and a measured high-water mark; the A/A noise-floor numbers; and matched-window fleet GPU-hour and token accounting, because benchmarks propose and production billing disposes.

Rollback gates, pre-committed. Revert if p95 TTFT or TPOT exceeds SLO at target concurrency; if any eval slice falls more than 1.0 point absolute with a 95% CI excluding zero; if structured-output compliance falls more than 2 points; if measured cost improvement is under 25%; if preemption or recompute rates rise without explanation; or if kernel-fallback evidence appears, in which case fix the tooling and re-run rather than concluding anything. Keep the BF16 arm warm and routable throughout so rollback is a routing flip rather than a redeploy, and rehearse the revert once before the canary.

Declared unknowns. Kernel efficiency on the specific shapes and TP degree in use, per-layer sensitivity of the specific checkpoint, and the production decode-token fraction are all MEASURED quantities in this design; none of them are asserted here. Every number above is labelled ESTIMATE and carries its derivation.

Analytical stance under test: kernel-dispatch-and-shape-coverage-first - a quantized kernel is fast only on the shapes it has a fast path for.

Falsifiable hypothesis H198c: the quantized kernel's fast path is dispatched for the batch sizes, sequence lengths and tensor shapes actually produced by production traffic, verified by logging the dispatched kernel name and its selection reason per shape across a replayed production trace. If a fallback path is dispatched for a material share of production shapes, the benchmarked speedup does not transfer to the served workload.

Quantized matrix-multiply kernels are not uniformly fast; they are collections of specialised implementations with shape constraints on batch dimension, hidden dimension alignment, group size and sometimes tile-friendly token counts, plus a generic fallback that can be slower than the unquantized baseline. A benchmark run at a single convenient batch size therefore measures one point of a highly non-uniform surface. Map the surface instead. Sweep the shapes that production actually produces, taken from the served batch-size and context-length distributions rather than from round numbers, and log for each shape the dispatched kernel name, whether it is the fast path or a fallback, and the achieved time; then weight the per-shape results by the production frequency of each shape to obtain a traffic-weighted speedup rather than a peak speedup. Two operational consequences follow. Continuous batching produces a wide and time-varying distribution of batch sizes, including many small odd-sized batches at low load and large batches at peak, so a kernel tuned for large aligned batches can leave the common case untouched or regressed, and the aggregate effect depends on the load profile rather than on the kernel's headline number. Autotuning and cache warmth matter: some kernel libraries select implementations by a first-call autotune whose results are cached per shape, so early requests after a restart pay a selection cost and rare shapes may never reach a tuned implementation, which shows up as tail latency rather than as mean regression. Boundary condition: at batch size one the operation is bandwidth-bound and the byte argument is strongest, while at large batch it becomes compute-bound and dequantization overhead can dominate, so the sign of the effect can flip within the served range and a single-number speedup is not well defined. ESTIMATE: the traffic-weighted speedup is the sum over shapes of production share times per-shape measured ratio, which can be far below the best-shape ratio when fallback dispatch covers common shapes; derivation is a frequency-weighted average over the measured shape sweep, and it is an ESTIMATE, not MEASURED. Analytical stance under test: decision-authority-and-conflict-of-interest-first - who is allowed to declare the comparison fair determines whether it is.

Falsifiable hypothesis H198j: the comparison's acceptance criteria, slice gates and stopping rule were registered before any measurement, and the party that ran the study is not the sole party authorised to declare it passed, testable by inspecting the pre-registration artefact's timestamp against the first measurement timestamp and the sign-off record. If criteria were set or revised after results were seen, or if the runner is the sole approver, the fairness claim is procedural rather than evidential.

Fairness in a cost-reduction comparison is as much a governance property as a measurement property, because the party proposing the saving usually also designs, runs and interprets the study, and every ambiguous methodological choice then has a direction that favours the proposal. Fix this structurally rather than by asking for care. Pre-register, with a timestamp that precedes the first measurement, the arm definitions, the fixed and varied factors, the primary metric and its SLO percentile, the per-slice quality gates and their tolerances, the noise-floor procedure, the sample size and stopping rule, and the explicit conditions that would constitute a negative result. Store that registration in the same versioned artefact as the results so a reader can diff intent against outcome, and require any deviation to be recorded as an amendment with a reason and a timestamp rather than silently applied. Separate the roles: the team that runs the study proposes, but sign-off requires the service owner who carries the SLO and, for anything touching user-visible quality, an independent reviewer who did not build the artefact. Require the negative case to be pre-specified so that a null result is publishable within the organisation rather than quietly abandoned, since selective reporting across many quantization attempts manufactures apparent wins from noise. Boundary condition: for a low-stakes internal service the full apparatus is disproportionate, and a lighter version, consisting of a written pre-registration and one independent reviewer, retains most of the protection; state which regime applies and why. ESTIMATE: with many uncontrolled analysis choices and selective reporting, the probability that at least one configuration shows a favourable result by chance rises quickly toward certainty, which is why the stopping rule and slice list must be fixed in advance; derivation is multiple-comparison inflation over the number of effectively independent choices, and it is an ESTIMATE, not MEASURED. Rollback gate: no adoption on a study whose acceptance criteria cannot be shown to predate its first measurement.



--- Shared substrate (identical across this study, stated once so the stance above is the only variable) ---

Mechanism. Weight-only quantization (WOQ) reduces the BYTES OF WEIGHTS READ PER FORWARD PASS. It therefore helps only where the kernel is memory-bandwidth bound, which in LLM serving means small-batch autoregressive decode. Prefill is compute bound; dequantization adds arithmetic there, so TTFT is flat or slightly worse. As batch size rises, decode GEMMs become compute bound too and the advantage decays monotonically toward 1.0x. Any claim of a uniform speedup across the concurrency range is mechanically wrong and should be treated as an instrumentation bug until explained.

Byte-count ceiling (ESTIMATE, derivation inline, not a throughput result). A 9B-parameter model in BF16 is 9e9 x 2 B = 18 GB of weights. INT4 with group-128 FP16 scale and zero point costs about 0.5 + ~0.06 B/param, i.e. ~5.0-5.3 GB. Ratio ~3.2-3.6x. This is pure byte counting with no kernel-efficiency model and no attention or KV traffic included; it is an upper bound on batch-1 decode speedup ONLY. Applying Amdahl with a decode-weight-read fraction f: f=0.4 bounds end-to-end gain near 1.33x, f=0.8 near 2.1x (ESTIMATE).

Mandatory two-arm-plus-one design. Run the quantized configuration TWICE: (a) with KV cache block count clamped to the BF16 baseline's block count, which isolates the kernel/bandwidth effect; (b) at native capacity, which shows the deployable benefit. Freed HBM becomes additional KV blocks and raises throughput by batching alone. If the clamped arm is flat, the honest conclusion is "we bought KV headroom", and tuning KV settings on the BF16 arm must be priced as the cheaper alternative before shipping a second numeric path.

Arm identity is frozen and hashed. Checkpoint hash, bit width, group size, symmetric/asymmetric, outlier or mixed-precision policy, calibration dataset hash, library and engine build, TP/PP layout, activation precision, KV precision, block size, max_num_seqs, max_model_len, chunked-prefill state, speculative-decoding state. The configuration symmetric difference between arms must be exactly the bit-width fields; anything else invalidates the comparison. Weight-only means weight-only: "INT4 plus FP8 KV" is two experiments, and the KV change usually explains most of the throughput delta while none of the quality delta gets attributed correctly.

Comparison point. Compare arms at the intersection of each arm's own latency-throughput frontier with the p95 SLO, never at a fixed batch size; the two arms have different optimal batch sizes, and fixed-batch comparison is the single most common way these studies mislead. Cost unit is GPU-seconds per 1,000 output tokens at that fixed p95 SLO, converted to currency last.

Measurement protocol. At least five concurrency points, at least three repeats per point, steady state with a fixed warmup-exclusion rule, greedy decoding and fixed seed for quality, bootstrap 95% CIs on ABSOLUTE quality deltas. Quality is sliced: long context, structured/JSON output, code, math, safety and refusal behaviour; aggregate scores can stay flat while repetition or truncation degrades, so sampled side-by-side output diffs are part of the evidence, not a nicety. A BF16-vs-BF16 A/A control across seeds and physical GPUs establishes the noise floor that any claimed delta must clear.

Confounders to control and report. Autotune cache warmth; clock and thermal drift over long runs; asymmetric telemetry overhead; prefill/decode mix drift between arms; silent kernel fallback to a dequantize-then-GEMM path (dump per-layer kernel names and timings and diff the arms - a null result with a fallback in the logs is a tooling defect, not a verdict on the method); calibration-set leakage into the eval set, disproved by hash comparison; library defaults silently changing group size across versions.

Evidence required before any decision. Per-request raw records (arrival, TTFT, per-token timestamps, output length, status); per-layer kernel name and achieved-bandwidth traces for both arms; the arm configuration manifest with hashes; per-slice quality scores with CIs plus raw generations; the HBM ledger with KV blocks as the residual and a measured high-water mark; the A/A noise-floor numbers; and matched-window fleet GPU-hour and token accounting, because benchmarks propose and production billing disposes.

Rollback gates, pre-committed. Revert if p95 TTFT or TPOT exceeds SLO at target concurrency; if any eval slice falls more than 1.0 point absolute with a 95% CI excluding zero; if structured-output compliance falls more than 2 points; if measured cost improvement is under 25%; if preemption or recompute rates rise without explanation; or if kernel-fallback evidence appears, in which case fix the tooling and re-run rather than concluding anything. Keep the BF16 arm warm and routable throughout so rollback is a routing flip rather than a redeploy, and rehearse the revert once before the canary.

Declared unknowns. Kernel efficiency on the specific shapes and TP degree in use, per-layer sensitivity of the specific checkpoint, and the production decode-token fraction are all MEASURED quantities in this design; none of them are asserted here. Every number above is labelled ESTIMATE and carries its derivation.
